Use --choice-description when a choice label alone does not explain its effect, and --recommended <label> for the recommended choice. Keep recommendation markers out of labels. The CLI now converts a trailing (recommended) or [recommended] into recommendation metadata and refuses conflicting recommendations.
Cursor sends now use its native conversation identifier when available. Older Cursor shells remain detection-only; asynchronous questions and notes still require a proven continuation route.
Cursor can receive Session Notes through a held native Stop continuation. OpenClaw native Codex shells retain their OpenClaw session identity.
Cursor Session Presence ends when its native agent exits, even if an intermediate hook shell remains alive.
A new Cursor prompt fences the previous held Stop before it can deliver another note.
Notifai no longer runs git where no repository can be found, so a Mac without the developer tools no longer offers to install them when Notifai checks setup. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

Setup reads more plainly. The computer-approval message an agent relays now tells the User to scan the QR code with their phone's camera, sign in with their email if asked, check the code and approve. Interactive `notifai init` asks about hooks, command approval and the skill only after the setup notification arrives. A Mac's default computer name drops `.local`, and a registered phone that cannot receive yet gets the one step it is missing. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

Setup now gives agents scripts for every moment that needs the User. Harness setup and recovery opens with "What to tell the User": short, named lines for installing, approving this computer, getting the phone app, allowing notifications on iPhone and Android, the hooks choices, Codex `/hooks` approval, a new Claude Code session and finishing, plus one recovery line for each common failure. Read it before your first setup message to the User and say the script for the current moment as written. The Codex `/hooks` request reads more plainly.

Setup no longer needs a plan; delivering notifications does. An Account without a plan can approve this computer, install the phone app and wire its harnesses, so `notifai init` now asks for the app first and reports the plan as the last step, in place of the test notification, which it does not send without a plan. `send` and `ask` refused for that reason print one line with the stable code `no_active_plan`: "Notifai needs an active plan to deliver notifications. Choose one at <plans page>". The `no-plan` setup script now says the same. A running Notifai no longer treats a missing plan as a refused credential: it keeps the computer paired and resumes once a plan is active.

Getting the phone app no longer opens a page on the computer. Interactive `notifai init` shows a QR in the terminal that a phone's camera opens straight to the App Store (iPhone) or the free Android test sign-up, with one line saying to sign in with the same email and allow notifications. The devices gap's remedy and `notifai devices` name the same two links, and `init --json` adds them to the devices gap as `technical.install_urls`. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

Every gap in `notifai init --json` now carries `message`: the exact line to send the User, written by the CLI for that gap. It covers approving this computer, getting the phone app, allowing notifications on iPhone and Android, a declined or expired approval, an unreachable service, an Account without a plan, Codex `/hooks` approval and an unconfirmed test notification; any other gap says what Notifai reported and what it asks for. States that need nothing from the User carry `null`. Harness setup and recovery now says: close a gap themselves when its remedy is a command they can run, otherwise send its `message` exactly as written, and keeps scripts only for the moments that are not gaps (installing, the approval link when the QR cannot be shown, the hooks choices, a new Claude Code session, finishing, and cloud or unknown computers). With an older Notifai that has no `message`, say what `remedy.summary` asks in plain words.

While an Account has no plan, `notifai init` counts a registered phone or desktop app that has notification permission as set up, so the plan is the one remaining step. A desktop app cannot keep its delivery stream open before a plan is active. Existing agent guidance is unchanged.

The setup notification is a confirmation, not a setup step. `notifai init --json` reports `ready: true` once this computer, the Project and a phone that can receive are set up, whether or not the app has confirmed the test notification. Until it confirms, the `proof` state is an optional gap with no `message`: it asks nothing of the User and never sets the exit code. Never wait for it or ask the User about it. Init sends it last, at most once per machine and phone, watches about 10 seconds for its receipt, and never re-sends it; a later run only reads whether it arrived. A test notification that cannot be sent, or whose delivery is rejected, is a real `proof` gap: its `message` asks the User to open the app so it can reconnect. Interactive `notifai init` asks about hooks, command approval and the skill once each, right after this computer is approved and before the phone step, the plan and the test notification. The `done` and `done-no-questions` scripts no longer say the app confirmed the test notification. An older Notifai can report `proof` as a gap and `ready: false` because of it alone; setup is done all the same.
Codex internal memory workspaces no longer activate Notifai. Requests from these folders are refused with codex_memory_workspace; normal Projects and other harnesses are unchanged.

Hook installation and discovery now follow shared configuration files in the selected harness home without replacing symlinks. Codex approval remains specific to the active home: open /hooks in a session using that same CODEX_HOME, even when its hook files are shared with another home. Existing approvals are never copied automatically.
